title: Funeral parades and the move to Chicago
summary: Taylor says funeral bands were only a New Orleans custom; a brief aside on his army service leads to his coming to Chicago.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: By the way, do you remember in any of your early days, any parades? Like in New Orleans, they used brass bands for funerals, too. You know, they still used those. They'll have the band out for a funeral. Did you ever?
I, I didn't, I didn't, I didn't, they didn't have that in Memphis. As I can remember, that was only happened in New Orleans.
But I wondered any other, or Texas, you don't remember ever any bands, funerals, that way?
Only when I came to Chicago, I played a few films with the band.
When did you come to Chicago? Yeah, in my... I don't want to skip over the rest of your life, you went over to Europe, too, didn't you? In the Army or something? In the Army, yeah.
